# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles WGS84 coordinates, active occupational spans and benchmark population series for 295 excavated settlements and camp complexes (795 settlement-year observations, 2,69 mean per settlement, 161 entries with >= 3 chronological observations) across Northern Plains Hydrological Unit 10 between 9900BC and 1600AD [@kelly2025; @bird2022p3k14c]. The inventory spans Palaeoindian and Early Archaic camps (La Sena, Big Eddy, Cherokee Sewer, Dent, Anzick, Lindenmeier, Agate Basin, Hell Gap), high-plains seasonal camps and horticultural outposts (Hagen, Boarding School Bison Drive, Wahkpa Chu'gn, Glenrock, Kobold, Kutoyis), fortified Middle Missouri and Oneota earthlodge towns (Blood Run, Sully, Double Ditch, Larson, On-A-Slant, Huff Indian Village, Big Hidatsa, Scattered Village, Crow Creek, Mitchell Prehistoric Village), and Lower Missouri, Central Plains and confluence centres (Utz, Utz Oneota Town, Mitchell, Paint Creek, Burkett, Big Osage Earthlodge Town, Wright, Steed-Kisker, El Quartelejo) [@frison1991prehistoric; @lehmer1971middle; @wedel1959kansas; @pauketat2004cahokia]. Source-ledger reconciliation confirms 295 included sites, 317 duplicate-alias exclusions within 2 km and 13 non-habitation exclusions, accounting for all 625 evaluated candidates with zero omissions.



# Background

Nucleated and seasonal habitations in Northern Plains HU 10 mirror the basin's east-to-west ecological gradient [@frison1991prehistoric; @wedel1959kansas]. On the western shortgrass plains and foothills of Montana, Wyoming and northern Colorado, early Palaeoindian and Archaic bands left stratified hunting camps at La Sena (9900BC to 9500BC, peak 40), Dent (9300BC to 8900BC, peak 45), Anzick (9100BC to 8900BC, peak 45), Lindenmeier (8900BC to 8400BC, peak 110), Hell Gap (9000BC to 3000BC, peak 95) and Agate Basin (8600BC to 7500BC, peak 95), followed in the late first and second millennia AD by high-plains occupation camps and drives including Wahkpa Chu'gn (peak 310), Boarding School Bison Drive (peak 340), Kutoyis (peak 250), Kobold (peak 240) and Glenrock (peak 260) alongside the Lower Yellowstone horticultural outpost at Hagen (peak 420) [@reher1980vore; @mulloy1942hagen].

Along the Middle Missouri Trench in South Dakota, North Dakota and northwestern Iowa, Mandan, Hidatsa and Initial Coalescent villagers erected densely packed earthlodge towns on river bluffs, frequently fortified with dry ditches and bastioned timber palisades [@lehmer1971middle; @wood1967huff; @willey1990crow]. Early Plains Village towns such as Mitchell Prehistoric Village (peak 720 in 1100AD) and Sommers (peak 880 in 1150AD) gave way after 1300AD to larger fortified towns including Huff Indian Village (1,35k), Double Ditch (1,85k), Larson (1,48k), On-A-Slant (1,45k), Big Hidatsa (1,32k) and Sully (2,65k), as well as the regional Oneota aggregation at Blood Run (3,5k).

Further south across Nebraska, Kansas, western Iowa and Missouri, early Mississippian-linked centres such as Mitchell on the eastern confluence seam (2,2k in 1100AD), Glenwood (880) and Steed-Kisker (680) transitioned into expansive protohistoric Oneota, Pawnee and Wichita river towns led by Utz (2,6k), Utz Oneota Town (1,8k), Paint Creek (1,62k), Burkett (1,48k), Big Osage Earthlodge Town (1,4k) and Wright (1,18k) [@alex2000iowa; @wedel1959kansas; @pauketat2004cahokia].

# Methodology

## Gazetteer Inclusion and Boundary Assignment

Candidate sites were evaluated under CENTAUR criteria requiring documented WGS84 coordinates, stratified radiocarbon or ceramic dating and quantifiable residential or seasonal camp estimates [@bird2022p3k14c; @kelly2025]. Unlike earlier stub inventories, the expanded 295-site gazetteer integrates well-dated Palaeoindian and Archaic occupations alongside Plains Woodland and Plains Village towns while excluding 13 unquantified non-habitation features (caves, rockshelters, mines, quarries, medicine wheels and major buffalo jumps such as First Peoples Buffalo Jump, Vore Buffalo Jump, Mummy Cave and Medicine Wheel-Bighorn) and consolidating 317 duplicate coordinate twins within 2 km in the regional source ledger. Frontier settlements on the eastern Missouri-Mississippi seam (Mitchell in Illinois) and along adjacent state borders are retained for smooth cross-frontier Matérn conditioning, with all benchmark years stamped in GMT+0.

## Earthlodge and Camp Population Estimation

Middle Missouri, Central Plains and Oneota town totals multiply excavated or magnetically surveyed earthlodge counts by mean household size (8-12 persons per lodge) and phase contemporaneity factors [@lehmer1971middle; @wood1967huff]. High-plains seasonal camp and Palaeoindian locality figures reflect peak seasonal residential congregations inferred from processing areas, hearth counts and camp scatter extent [@reher1980vore; @frison1991prehistoric].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation confirms 295 included sites matching the settlement gazetteer (795 benchmark observations) and 330 excluded entries (317 duplicate-alias consolidations within 2 km plus 13 unquantified non-habitation exclusions), reconciling all 625 candidates in the regional source ledger with zero discrepancy. Chronological checks confirm the west-to-east settlement shift (Table \ref{tab:coverage-sett-northern-plains}): 133 sites sit in the Middle Missouri Trench (45,1%) and 132 in the Platte-Republican-Lower Missouri Prairie-Plains (44,7%), compared with 15 in Upper Missouri Montana (5,1%) and 15 in the Wyoming Basin (5,1%). Early village peaks at Mitchell (2,2k in 1100AD), Mitchell Prehistoric Village (720 in 1100AD) and Steed-Kisker (680 in 1200AD) precede the protohistoric 1600AD maxima at Blood Run (3,5k), Sully (2,65k), Utz (2,6k), Double Ditch (1,85k) and Paint Creek (1,62k) [@wood1967huff; @alex2000iowa; @wedel1959kansas].

# Results

## Leading Settlement Gazetteer

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-northern-plains} lists the Top 45 settlements by peak population descending out of the 295 catalogued sites across HU 10, and Figure \ref{fig:settlements-northern-plains} plots the rank-size curve dominated by Blood Run (3,5k), Sully (2,65k), Utz (2,6k), Mitchell (2,2k), Double Ditch (1,85k), Utz Oneota Town (1,8k) and Paint Creek (1,62k).

# Limitations

Three constraints govern HU 10 site data. First, frontier boundary conditioning retains Mitchell on the Illinois confluence seam (2,2k in 1100AD); in continental CENTAUR compilation, cross-border settlements are deduplicated deterministically without double counting [@pauketat2004cahokia]. Second, Crow Creek reflects a single catastrophic 1300AD fortification and massacre horizon (850 inhabitants) rather than a multi-century town occupation [@willey1990crow; @bamforth2018warfare]. Third, 13 unquantified caves, rockshelters, mines, quarries, medicine wheels and major buffalo jumps (including First Peoples Buffalo Jump, Vore Buffalo Jump, Mummy Cave and Medicine Wheel-Bighorn) are excluded in the regional source ledger, whereas quantified seasonal bison-drive and foothill occupation camps (Boarding School Bison Drive, Glenrock, Wahkpa Chu'gn) represent peak seasonal congregations rather than permanent year-round residency [@reher1980vore].
